title: Clean old thermal paste off a desktop CPU's heat spreader with an alcohol wipe
instruction: Clean the old thermal paste off the processor's heat spreader with the alcohol wipe, leaving it dry and lint-free.
context: A routine PC-building and repair step: after lifting a cooler, the old thermal paste has to come off the processor's nickel heat spreader before fresh paste goes on. The usual tools are 91% isopropyl alcohol and a folded lint-free wipe (Kimtech W4/Kimwipes class), worked in small circles over the lid, with the socket frame, load plate, lever and the CPU's pin field kept clean and the lid left unscratched; then the IPA is allowed to flash off. The job is done by computer repair technicians (BLS 49-2012, about 100,000 US jobs), computer hardware engineers (17-2061, about 80,000) and system integrators, and it is a familiar step to anyone who has repasted a desktop. The sim slows nothing and reduces no force: the pad's contact and rubbing are the solver's, and the no-touch zones are the real socket parts.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A 500 x 440 x 3 mm dark anti-static mat is centred at (0.36, -0.07). On it, a 305 x 244 x 1.6 mm ATX motherboard (dark-green PCB, nine 6.5 mm brass standoffs) is fixed with its CPU socket at (0.36, -0.07); the board top is 11.1 mm above the table. The socket is a black 54 x 54 mm AM4 frame with a 40.2 mm opening, a steel load plate on the substrate edge (top 14.55 mm), a steel lever along +x with a plastic grip (top 16.8 mm) and four brass-lined 54 x 90 mm cooler holes. An AM4-class CPU is fixed in it: 40 x 40 mm dark-green substrate, 37.5 x 37.5 x 3.6 mm nickel-plated copper IHS with a 0.15 mm chamfer, copper foot, etched lid, pin-1 triangle and gold edge traces; the IHS top is 18.45 mm above the table. The old paste is a 30 x 20 mm, 0.05 mm, 0.08 g grey patch of 122 2 x 2 mm cells on the IHS centre (top 18.475 mm), fixed to the CPU. A folded 50 x 50 x 2 mm white 91% IPA lint-free wipe (24 x 24 mm contact face standing 0.8 mm proud of the flange) is on a 40 x 40 x 6 mm dark-blue backing with a 20 x 20 x 26 mm grip bar, contact face at z 6.0 mm, centred in the 80 x 80 x 3 mm blue foil tray at (0.24, -0.24); its total mass is 27.5 g and it carries 1.5 mL of 91% IPA. An empty 80 x 80 x 3 mm grey waste tray is at (0.46, -0.24). A 4 g grey paste tube lies at (0.18, 0.10), the CPU's black 60 x 60 x 28 mm box at (0.56, 0.10), a red-handled Phillips #2 screwdriver at (0.54, -0.16), a folded-wipe foil packet at (0.15, -0.02) and a 90 x 140 mm anti-static bag at (0.14, -0.06). The motherboard, socket, CPU, paste, bench, trays and props are fixed; the wipe is the only free body.
scoring: The paste is a 122-cell, 2 mm coverage layer on the IHS. A cell is removed only on real contact and rubbing: the wipe's soft face must be on the IHS (the live pad-CPU normal force at least 0.12 N, the face flat within 20 degrees), the pad must have moved at least 0.2 mm across the lid since the previous 0.05 s control step, and the wipe must be wet (wetness above 0.10). A wipe hovering 1 mm above, held still on the lid, or dragged off the lid removes nothing. The wipe starts wet (1.5 mL of 91% IPA) and loses wetness in contact; a dry wipe removes nothing and leaves lint. The score is 0 until a gripper holds the wipe by its 20 mm bar (16-24 mm opening, a real grip force) and it has been wet; then 0.25. It is 0.5 once at least 60 % of the cells are clean, 0.75 once at least 95 % are clean, and 1.0 when every cell is clean, the IPA film is dry (max cell wetness <= 0.05), there is no lint, no paste on the socket/pins (no pad contact with the board or with the CPU outside the IHS), no scratch (no hard part on the CPU, no dry press over 2 N, no wet press over 6 N, no lean over 25 degrees with over 0.5 N), the wipe is below its 0.12 g paste load, and the wipe and both grippers are at least 6 cm from the CPU for a 1 s hold. A clean cell has less than 2 % of its paste left. Caps: paste on the socket/pins caps the run at 0.25; a scratch caps it at 0.5; a wipe loaded above 0.12 g redeposits 0.30 paste fraction on clean cells and caps the run at 0.5. The caps apply after the ladder. The full score must hold for 1 s with the wipe still within 2 mm and 2 degrees; the CPU is fixed. The real station reads the same ladder: the IHS under a raking light and a loupe for paste and scratches, the socket/load plate/lever/pins for paste, the wipe's soiled face and a white final wipe for redeposit/lint, and the IHS dry after 2-5 minutes.
reset_notes: Put a fresh folded 50 x 50 mm 91% IPA lint-free wipe on its foil tray at (0.24, -0.24), bar up, with 1.5 mL of IPA. Re-apply the 30 x 20 mm, 0.05 mm, 0.08 g grey paste patch (122 cells) on the cleaned IHS; the CPU stays in its socket and the board stays fixed. Empty the waste tray and discard or place the used wipe in it. Check the socket frame, load plate, lever and the CPU's pin field are clean and dry. The simulator resets the wipe's IPA and the paste cells; the real station is reset as above.
fidelity: REAL: AM4 40x40 mm package, IHS 37.5x37.5x3.6 mm; 54x54 mm socket; folded 91% IPA wipe, 1.5 mL; 30x20 0.08 g paste. Pad force/motion from the solver: 0.12 N min, flat within 20 deg, 0.2 mm rubbing, 122-cell 2 mm grid. DECLARED: socket body, IHS thickness, paste mass, wipe 2.5 g + 25 g applicator (grip only), capacity 0.12 g, wetness/dry time, 0.10 wetness, 6 N wet/2 N dry scratch, 25 deg lean. Scratch/lint/pin rules declared; real checks are raking light, loupe, white wipe and socket inspection.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the policy never picks the wipe). Demo: 1.0 at step 658 on Isaac (PhysX contact) and MuJoCo (122/122 clean, dry, 1 s hold). Pytest 17.
